name: OH-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a PVI of R+15
Balderson's large financial advantage ($2.0M cash vs $19K)
Incumbency advantage in a low-profile race
Prediction markets price Democratic chances near 4%
model.rationale: The R+15 district lean, Balderson's incumbency and roughly 20-to-1 cash advantage over Jerrad Christian, and markets pricing his win odds above 90% all point to a comfortable Republican hold, with no polls or expert ratings suggesting movement toward the challenger.
model.watch: A surge of outside spending or polling showing Christian within single digits would be the first sign this race deserves a second look.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Troy Balderson seeks another term in a central Ohio district that leans heavily Republican, with a partisan baseline of roughly fifteen points in the GOP's favor. He enters the general election with a commanding financial position, holding nearly $2 million on hand after raising $1.7 million, while Democrat Jerrad Christian has raised under $85,000 and has about $19,000 available. No independent polls or expert race ratings are available for this contest, and prediction markets give Balderson roughly a 94% chance of winning.

The fundamentals leave little room for doubt: the district lean, incumbency, and the money gap all point the same direction. Christian would need an unusual wave environment and outside resources to make this competitive, and there is no evidence of either so far. The seat remains safely in Republican hands heading into November.
